For neither of these two is a decisive text (nass) on the generality of the word "ma," just as the first is a decisive text on its specificity. The ruling of a text extending to something does not require that it extend to it by way of the expression ('ibara, the literal meaning). It suffices for that that it extends to them by way of indication of the text (dalalat al-nass, the implied meaning), through the shared quality of being worshipped besides Allah, the Exalted. So perhaps the Prophet (ﷺ), after explaining the meaning of the noble wording by what he mentioned, and that those mentioned were not included in its ruling by way of expression, also explained that they were not included in it by way of indication, as an emphasis on the refutation and the obligation, and a repetition of the rebuke and the silencing. But this is not based on their being objects of worship for those who worship them, as they claim. For removing some of the objects of worship from a ruling that signals anger toward both the worshippers and the worshipped would create the impression of a permission to worship in general. Rather, it is based on establishing the truth and clarifying that they have no part in worship at all, so that it cannot be imagined that they enter the ruling by indication, due to their sharing with the idols in being worshipped besides Allah, the Exalted. Their deity is actually the devils who ordered them to worship them, as expressed by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to You! You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn...﴾ to the end of the verse. Thus, they are the ones included in the stated ruling, because they share with the idols in being worshipped besides Him, the Exalted, unlike those mentioned, peace be upon them. This is the way to reconcile the reports mentioned. As for generalizing the word "ma" to rational beings as well, and making what comes later in His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has preceded﴾ ... to the end, an explanation of a figurative usage (tajawwuz) or a specification (takhsis), it is something that the context and the flow of the discourse do not support, as sound taste testifies.

Al-hasab (fuel): that which is thrown in and which kindles the fire, from "hasabahu" when he pelted him with pebbles. It has also been read with a sukun on the sad (ḥaṣab), as a descriptive adjective of it using the verbal noun, for emphasis.

﴿You are its arrivers﴾ is either a resumptive new sentence or a substitute for ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾. The lam here substitutes for ʿalā (upon), to indicate exclusivity, and that their coming to it is for its sake. The address is to them and to what they worship, by way of predominance (taghlib, giving precedence to the masculine rational group in address).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 99:

﴿Had these been gods﴾, i.e., their idols, ﴿as they claim, they would not have entered it﴾. And since their entering it has been shown, it is necessarily established that they cannot be gods. This, as you see, is clear that what is meant by "those whom they worship" is the idols, because the purpose is to establish the opposite of what they claim. They claim the divinity of the idols, not the divinity of the devils, so that it could be argued from their entering the Fire that they are not gods. As for what occurred in the noble hadith, it occurred by way of supplement, as the discourse was led to it while explaining what the noble text was brought for, by way of allusion. For Ibn al-Za'abari asked about the state of all the other objects of worship, and confining the answer to the first reply would give the impression of permission to worship them in general, since they are worshipped by them. So he was answered by clarifying that the objects of worship are the devils and that they are included in the ruling of the text, but by way of allusion, lest there be a contradiction between the two reports (khabar).

﴿And each﴾, i.e., of the worshippers and the worshipped, ﴿will abide therein forever﴾, having no escape from it.

"For them therein is zafir" — that is, moaning and intense exhaling of breath. And although this is among the actions of the worshippers, it is attributed to all (of them) by way of prevailing (al-taghlib). It is also permissible that the pronoun refers to the worshippers, since there is no ambiguity (li-adam al-ilbas). Likewise in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they therein do not hear﴾ — that is, some of them do not hear the moaning of others, because of the intensity of the terror and the horribleness of the punishment. It has also been said: they do not hear what would gladden them of speech.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 101:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) from Us has already preceded﴾ This begins an explanation of the state of the believers, following the explanation of the state of the disbelievers, in accordance with the customary practice of the revelation of pairing promise with threat and presenting encouragement alongside warning. That is: the best quality from Us has already preceded for them in the decree, which is the best of qualities, namely happiness (al-sa'ada). It has also been said: it is divine success (al-tawfiq) in obedience. Or: Our word of good tidings of reward for obedience has preceded for them. The latter is the more inclusive and the more apparent in bearing upon it, because the first two, despite their obscurity, are not among the things within the capacity of the accountable.

So this sentence, together with what follows it, is a detailed explanation of what was stated in summary in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no denial of his effort, and indeed We are recording it for him﴾. Likewise, what precedes it, from the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿"Indeed, you and what you worship..."﴾ and so on, is a detailed explanation of what was stated in summary in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿"And prohibited is..."﴾ and so on.

﴿Those﴾ is a demonstrative referring to the relative pronoun, in view of its being characterized by what is within the scope of the relative clause, and the sense of distance in it indicates the elevation of their rank and the remoteness of their station in nobility and excellence. That is: those described with the beautiful attribute that has been mentioned.

﴿From it﴾, that is, from Hell, ﴿will be kept far away﴾, because they are in Paradise, and how vast is the difference between it and the Fire.

As for what has been narrated, that 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) once delivered a sermon, recited this verse, and then said: "I am among them, and Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Sa'id, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and Abu 'Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, may the pleasure of Allah the Exalted be upon them all." Then the prayer was established, and he rose dragging his garment.

"And he says: ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ — this is not explicit evidence that the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) refers to a specific group. Al-hasis is a sound that is perceived, meaning they will not hear its sound with a faint hearing, as is customary when the one making the sound is far away, even though its sound is extremely loud; not that they will not hear its hidden sound in itself only. The clause is either a substitute (badal) for "those who have been kept far away" (mub'adun), or a circumstantial clause (hal) from their pronoun, brought for the sake of emphasis on their deliverance from it.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾ is an explanation of their attainment of their desires, following the explanation of their deliverance from destructions and calamities; that is: they will remain eternally in the utmost comfort. The fronting of the adverbial phrase (zarf) serves to restrict and to give it emphasis."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 103:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾, is an explanation of their deliverance from terror altogether, after the explanation of their deliverance from the Fire, because if the greatest of terrors does not grieve them, then by necessity nothing else besides it will grieve them. On the authority of al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: it is the departure toward the Fire. On the authority of al-Dahhak: until it closes over the Fire. It has also been said: it is when Death is slaughtered in the form of a white-and-black ram. And it has been said: it is the final blast, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will be terrified﴾. But this is not the case, for the one who is safe from that terror is the one whom Allah, exalted is He, has excepted by His saying: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, not all the believers described by good deeds. Moreover, most scholars hold that this (terror) is at the first blast, not the final one, as will come in (Surat al-Naml).

﴿And the angels will meet them﴾, i.e., they will receive them, congratulating them: ﴿This is your day﴾, by way of implying a saying, i.e., saying: this day is your day ﴿which you were promised﴾ in the world, and you were given good news of the various kinds of rewards therein for faith and acts of obedience. This, as you see, is clear that what is meant by those ﴿for whom the good reward has preceded﴾ (p-88) is all the believers described by faith and good deeds, not only those mentioned from al-Masih, 'Uzayr and the angels, peace be upon them, specifically, as has been said.

﴿On the day We roll up the heaven﴾ (nūn al-ʿaẓama, the "we" of majesty) is in the accusative, governed by "udhkur" (remember). It has also been said that it is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) for His words ﴿the terror will not grieve them﴾. It has also been said that it is governed by "tatalaqqāhum" (the angels will receive them), and it has also been said that it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) that is implied, from the omitted pronoun in "tūʿadūn" (you are promised). Ṭayy is the opposite of nashr (spreading out), and it has been said that it means effacement (maḥw). It was also read as "yuṭwā" with the yāʾ and with the tāʾ, in the passive form.

﴿Like the rolling of the scroll﴾. The sijill is the page (ṣaḥīfa). That is, rolling it up like the rolling of the ṭuwwāmār (a large scroll or ledger). It was read as "al-sajl" like the word "al-dalw" (bucket), and with a kasra. "Al-Sujull," on the pattern of "al-ʿutull," is also a form; these are two dialects. The lām in His words ﴿for the books﴾ is connected to an omitted element that is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of "al-sijill," or a qualifier of it according to the view of those who permit omitting the relative pronoun together with part of its relative clause; that is, "like the rolling of the scroll, being for the books," or "the one being for the books." The books are an expression for the pages and what is written in them, so the scroll is part of their parts, and rolling is truly connected to it. It was also read as "lilkitāb" (for the writing). This is either a verbal noun (maṣdar), with the lām expressing purpose, meaning "just as the ṭuwwāmār is rolled up for writing," or a noun like "al-imām," in which case the lām is as mentioned first. It was said that al-Sijill is the name of an angel who rolls up the books of the deeds of the children of Adam when they are raised up to him. It was also said that he is a scribe of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾. That is, We will repeat what We created as a beginning, a repetition like Our beginning of it in being brought into existence after non-existence, or in gathering together the scattered parts. The purpose is to show the validity of resurrection by analogy with the origin, because of the inclusion of the intrinsic possibility (imkān dhātī) that makes something capable of being willed, and because power extends equally to both. "Mā" is either a particle of restriction (kāffa) or a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyya). "Awwal" is an object of "bada'nā," or of a verb implied and explained by "nuʿīduhu." Or it is a relative pronoun, and the kāf is connected to an omitted element explained by "nuʿīduhu," meaning "We will repeat the like of that which We began." "Awwal khalq" is an adverb of time for "bada'nā," or a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of the omitted relative pronoun.

﴿A promise﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing its verb and confirming "nuʿīduhu," or it is in the accusative governed by it, because it is a promise of repetition.

﴿upon Us﴾, that is, it is incumbent upon Us to fulfil it, ﴿indeed We are ever doers﴾ of what has been mentioned, without doubt.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 105:

﴿And We have certainly written in the Zabur﴾: it is the Book of Dawud (David), upon him be peace. It has also been said that it is a term for the category of what was revealed to the Prophets, upon them be peace.

﴿after the Reminder﴾: that is, the Torah. It has also been said that it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). The meaning is: "And by Allah, We have certainly written in the Book of Dawud after We wrote in the Torah," or "We have written in all the revealed Books, after We had written and established it in the Preserved Tablet."

﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾: that is, the generality of the believers after the expulsion of the disbelievers. This is a promise from Him, exalted is He, of making the religion victorious and exalting its people. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that what is meant is the earth of Paradise, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to settle in Paradise wherever we will"﴾. It has also been said that it is the Holy Land, which the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) will inherit.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 106:

﴿Indeed, in this﴾ — i.e., in what has been mentioned in this noble surah of reports, profound admonitions, promise and warning, and decisive proofs indicating the Oneness of God (tawhid) and the soundness of prophethood — ﴿is indeed a message (balaghan)﴾ — i.e., sufficiency, or a means of reaching the desired goal — ﴿for a people who worship﴾ — i.e., for a people whose concern is worship rather than custom.

**﴿And We have not sent you﴾**, meaning with what has been mentioned, along with its like among the laws and rulings and other matters that are the basis for the happiness of both abodes.

**﴿except as a mercy to the worlds﴾**. It is in the accusative position (حيز النصب), as an exception (استثناء) from the most general causes (أعمّ العلل) or from the most general circumstances (أعمّ الأحوال). That is: We did not send you with what has been mentioned for any cause except by Our all-encompassing mercy to all the worlds; or, We did not send you in any circumstance except in the circumstance of being a mercy to them. For what you were sent with is a cause of the happiness of both abodes and a source of the ordering of their interests in both lives. Whoever does not seize the benefits of its effects has only neglected himself and the sanctity of his own right, not that God Most High has deprived him of what would make him happy. It has also been said that his being a mercy with regard to the disbelievers is that he secures them from being swallowed up by the earth, transformed, or utterly destroyed, as indicated by the words of God Most High: ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 108:

﴿Say: It is only revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ That is: what is revealed to me is only that there is no god for you except one God, because this is the primary purpose of the mission (al-ba'tha), whereas everything else is among the rulings that branch off from it. The particle innama in the first instance is for restricting a judgement to a thing (qasr al-hukm 'ala al-shay'), like your saying: "innama yaqumu Zayd" (only Zayd stands), meaning: no one stands except Zayd. The second instance is for restricting a thing to a judgement (qasr al-shay' 'ala al-hukm), like your saying: "innama Zayd qa'im" (Zayd is only standing), meaning: he has no attribute except the attribute of standing.

﴿So will you submit?﴾ That is: will you be sincere in worship to God, Exalted is He, dedicating worship to Him alone? The fa' (so) indicates that what precedes it necessitates what follows it. They said: in this there is an indication that the attribute of oneness (al-wahdaniyya) may be known through revelation (al-sam').

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 21, verse 109:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from Islam and do not heed what revelation requires of them. ﴿Then say﴾ to them: ﴿I have announced to you﴾, i.e., I have informed you of what I was commanded, or of my war against you, ﴿on equal terms﴾, meaning: being on equal terms in the announcement of it, in that I have not concealed it from any one of you; or being equal with you in it, both I and you in knowledge of what I have informed you of, or in enmity; or as an announcement on equal terms. It has also been said: I have informed you that I am on equal terms, i.e., with justice and uprightness of opinion through clear proof.

﴿And I do not know﴾, i.e., I do not know ﴿whether what you are promised is near or far﴾ of the victory of the Muslims and the manifestation of the religion, or the Resurrection, although it is certainly coming.

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken aloud⁠﻿﻿ of speech﴾: that is, what you openly declare of disparagement of Islam and denial of the verses, among which are those that speak of the coming of the promised one.

﴿And He knows what you conceal﴾ of rancor and malice toward the Muslims, and He will requite you for it, even to the extent of a speck (naqir) or a flimsy membrane (qitmir).

ران ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ means: I do not know; perhaps the delay of your recompense is a gradual leading-on (istidraj) for you and an increase in your being tempted, or it is a test for you, so that He may see how you act.

﴿And an enjoyment for a time﴾ means: and a provision for you until a determined term, which His will requires, will being founded upon far-reaching wisdoms, so that this may be a proof against you.

(p-90)﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth."﴾ This is a report of his (ﷺ) supplication. It was also read as "Say, 'My Lord,'" in the imperative form (ṣīghat al-amr), meaning: judge between us and the people of Makkah with the justice that calls for hastening the punishment and severity against them. His (ﷺ) supplication was answered when they were punished at Badr with a severe punishment. It was also read as "Rabbu" (with a ḍammah on the bā'), "Judge," and as "Rabbī aḥkamu" in the comparative form (ṣīghat al-tafḍīl), meaning "My Lord is more judicious," from al-iḥkām.

﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful﴾: this is the subject (mubtada'), meaning abundant in mercy toward His servants. Allah's words ﴿the One whose help is sought﴾ mean the one from whom help is requested, and this is another predicate (khabar) of the subject. The attribution of "Lord" in what preceded to his (ﷺ) pronoun alone is because supplication is one of the duties specific to him (ﷺ). Likewise, its attribution here to the plural pronoun, which includes the believers, is because seeking help is also one of the general duties of them.

﴿Against what you describe﴾: this refers to the state of affairs. They used to say that the power would be theirs, that the banner of Islam would flutter and then become stagnant, and that if what was threatened were true it would have descended upon them, and other such things in which there is no good. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, answered the supplication of His Messenger (ﷺ), frustrated their hopes, changed their conditions, and granted victory to His friends over them, so that on the Day of Badr what befell them befell them. The sentence is a concluding parenthetical clause (i'tirāḍ tadhyīlī) affirming the content of what precedes it. It was also read as "yaṣifūna" with a yā' (third person).

And from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Whoever recites Iqtaraba, Allah will call him to account with an easy reckoning, he will shake hands with him, and every prophet whose name is mentioned in the Qur'an will greet him with peace.﴾
